missionPremise: H1: measure the Hays place_key set (parcel_record) as a real id-set intersection against the cad_property account set, and declare a disposition (never-an-account / left-the-roll / different-key / unknown) for every non-intersecting row. Must land before any Hays cell fill. Heavy P-124 precedent already exists (CTX-HAYS-KEY, -REBIND, -BACKFILL, -SPLIT in legacy-design-tools; CTX-HAYS-GATE in this repo) establishing the root mechanism: for Hays, txgio_parcel.prop_id is the CAD QuickRefID R-account stem with the R stripped, a DIFFERENT numbering than cad_property.prop_id (the CAD PropertyID); a 2026-08-25 StratMap merge (P-78) padded cad_property with rows keyed on the TxGIO/StratMap numbering, overwriting source_file in place. This lane's job is narrower: build the measurement AS A DURABLE INSTRUMENT IN HAUSKA-FACTORY, because plan-progress.mjs's own CODE_PREDICATES list names H1 as checked 'in hauska-factory, its own instrument' rather than by SQL ledger query -- this is not optional framing, it is how the plan's own completion gate reads H1.

theVacuityFinding.whatANaiveTestSays: parcel_record.prop_id = ANY(cad_property.prop_id), raw string equality, county-wide, any cad_property vintage: Hays 116,420 of 116,420 parcel_record rows (100.00%) intersect. Bastrop 62,256 of 62,256 (100.00%) intersect. Read naively, H1's own completion predicate ('count of rows with no disposition == 0') would ALREADY read DONE with zero rows needing a disposition -- a false pass.
theVacuityFinding.whyItIsFalse: cad_property.prop_id is not one keyspace. The 2026-08-25 P-78 StratMap merge (per the dispatch's own STANDING FACTS) inserted geometry rows into cad_property KEYED ON TXGIO'S OWN prop_id (confirmed: cad_property source_file='stratmap25-landparcels_48209_lp.zip' has exactly 116,421 rows, one more than parcel_record's 116,420 -- consistent with a near-total copy of the same txgio-keyed population into cad_property by construction). So cad_property.prop_id today is the UNION of {real CAD PropertyIDs} union {TxGIO/StratMap prop_ids that were grafted in under their own numbering}. Testing parcel_record.prop_id against that union necessarily reads ~100% intersecting regardless of whether any REAL CAD account backs it -- this is the exact 'vacuous write path' shape the canon preamble names: it runs, it reports full coverage, and it cannot detect the defect on any input, because the comparison set was contaminated by the same graft that created the defect.
theVacuityFinding.theFix: the 'cad_property account set' must mean REAL CAD-SOURCED ACCOUNTS, not every row in the table. CTX-HAYS-SPLIT already calibrated the discriminator for Hays specifically: assessed_value IS NOT NULL. (The generic A-115 rule used elsewhere in this repo -- land_value>0 OR land_acres>0 -- is ALSO fooled for Hays: CTX-HAYS-GATE's own close proved TxGIO's Hays shapefile mapper DOES populate land_value/market_value/improvement_value from the shapefile's own attributes, only assessed_value is hardcoded null by that mapper. Verified live this session: applying the A-115 filter to Hays leaves 167,886 of 173,050 rows as 'real', which still reads ~100% intersecting with parcel_record -- the A-115 rule is the WRONG discriminator for this county and would have reproduced the same false pass. Applying assessed_value IS NOT NULL instead gives 134,990 real accounts and drops the naive intersection from 100.00% to 67.31% -- this is the first number in this lane that actually moves.)
theVacuityFinding.reconciliationWithPriorLanes: 38,059 Hays parcel_record rows fail to intersect the real-account set under this corrected test. CTX-HAYS-SPLIT's independently-derived 'geometryOnlyAbsentNoCadSignal' population is 38,060 (off by one). CTX-HAYS-GATE's independently-derived cadRoll-postcondition miss population is 38,197 (same shape, slightly different denominator -- CTX-HAYS-GATE compared cad_property's own 2025-vs-2026 vintage gap, not parcel_record). Three different instruments, three different repos/angles, converging within single digits to low hundreds on what is evidently the same underlying population. Not presented as exact agreement -- the denominators differ (parcel_record's txgio-sourced population vs cad_property's own vintage anti-join) -- but the convergence is strong enough to treat this as the same defect, not a coincidence, per DEV_PROCESS 1.4.

controlCountyFinding.dispatchsImpliedControl: Bastrop, per STANDING FACTS ('Bastrop was zero across 400 samples' on the 2026-09-03 StratMap-reload id-stability measurement).
controlCountyFinding.verifiedAtSourceAndFoundNotUsableAsAPosi: STANDING FACTS' Bastrop claim is about id STABILITY across a reload (a longitudinal, same-source comparison) -- a different measurement than this lane's cross-identifier comparison (does the txgio-sourced parcel_record population correspond to REAL cad_property accounts at all). Measured live: Bastrop's txgio_parcel table has exactly 62,257 distinct prop_id, ALL of them from source_file stratmap25-landparcels_48021_lp.zip. Bastrop's REAL CAD roll (DATA-EXPORT-01.14.2026.zip, 15,542 rows, 100% carrying assessed_value) has ZERO overlap with txgio_parcel.prop_id -- 0 of 15,542. Consequence: Bastrop's parcel_record (62,256 rows, all txgio-sourced) has ZERO structural path to ANY real Bastrop CAD account today -- not a wrong-key COLLISION like Hays, but a total absence of geometric linkage between Bastrop's real roll and its txgio/geometry table. By the same corrected test this lane applies to Hays, Bastrop would show 100% non-intersecting, not 0%, and its StratMap rows carry NO land/market/improvement value at all (real(assessed)=0 on that source -- genuinely hollow, unlike Hays' StratMap rows, 75,551 of which DO carry values via the P-78 coalesce-and-overwrite mechanism CTX-HAYS-KEY documented). Bastrop is therefore a real, differently-shaped defect (pure coverage gap, no false-positive risk) and NOT usable as a 'this should come back clean' positive control for the disposition classifier.
controlCountyFinding.whatIsUsedInstead: Caldwell (48055), on CTX-HAYS-SPLIT's own precedent (which hit and documented this exact same Bastrop-control failure for a related-but-different measurement and substituted Caldwell). Verified live: Caldwell's txgio_parcel has 24,989 distinct prop_id (source stratmap25-landparcels_48055_lp.zip); of Caldwell's 48,382 real (assessed_value not null) accounts, 24,722 (51.1%) ARE present as a txgio_parcel.prop_id -- a genuine, coherent, non-colliding numbering (Caldwell's real CAD PropertyID and its txgio prop_id are the SAME scheme, unlike Hays' two-namespace collision). This makes Caldwell usable two ways: (a) a TRUE-POSITIVE check -- the classifier must resolve a Caldwell row that already raw-matches as 'intersecting', never route it into the disposition path at all; (b) a TRUE-NEGATIVE check on the crosswalk step -- Caldwell's own genuinely-uncovered residue (roughly half its roll has no txgio geometry yet) must NOT be misclassified as 'different-key' by a classifier that is too eager to find a match. Bastrop is kept in the run as a THIRD, differently-shaped case specifically because its near-total absence-of-linkage is a clean test that the classifier does not manufacture false 'different-key' resolutions when a crosswalk genuinely cannot resolve anything -- it must fall through to never-an-account/unknown, not invent a match.
controlCountyFinding.additionalLiveFinding_dormantTable: migrations/bake/0005b_landing_cad_txgio_alias.sql defines landing_cad_txgio_alias specifically as a CAD<->TxGIO identity alias table with an owners_agree=TRUE quality gate and a valid_to temporal column -- exactly shaped to answer this lane's 'different-key' and 'left-the-roll' questions directly, without re-deriving a crosswalk. Checked live on BOTH staging and production: 0 rows, either store. A schema-ready, never-populated table; no writer for it exists anywhere in this repo (not chased further -- out of this lane's scope, flagged as a leave-behind). Its absence is why this lane must build its own crosswalk from the public CAD export, reusing the method CTX-HAYS-KEY/-REBIND already validated (self-tested, violation-tested, CI-green in legacy-design-tools#653) rather than inventing a new one.

fourBucketsPerTheDispatchsOwnVocabulary: different-key: the crosswalk (QuickRefID R-stem restricted to R-accounts, corroborated by PropertyNumber-to-txgio-geo_id, both derived from the county's own public CAD export, same method CTX-HAYS-REBIND validated) resolves this txgio prop_id to a specific CAD PropertyID. Positive, named, reproducible.

left-the-roll: reserved for a prop_id with POSITIVE historical evidence of prior CAD-account status that no longer resolves under any current identifier. Pre-registered expectation: this bucket will be small-to-empty for parcel_record's txgio-sourced population, because the only historical crosswalk source this program has (landing_cad_txgio_alias) is empty, and a single current-snapshot export cannot by itself prove a PRIOR resolution existed and has since closed. Reported as a finding, not forced to be non-empty.

never-an-account: a positive-ish signal that no CAD identity was ever assigned -- txgio_parcel's own geo_id is null/blank for this prop_id (the GIS source itself never geo-identified the feature, consistent with a non-parcel feature: ROW, water, easement sliver) AND no crosswalk resolution exists.

unknown: everything else that resists a positive call -- e.g. an ambiguous crosswalk (the R-stem and geo_id paths disagree on which PropertyID), or a populated geo_id with no resolving export row. Legitimate and must stay countable per the dispatch's own text; not a failure state.
dispositionDesign.preRegisteredExpectation: different-key dominates (>90% of the non-intersecting population), matching CTX-HAYS-KEY's own 38,200/38,444 = 99.37% finding for the closely related cad_property-side measurement. left-the-roll near zero. never-an-account and unknown split the small remainder. Stated before the classifier runs; a result outside this band is reported as a finding either way, not smoothed toward it.
dispositionDesign.violationPlan: self-test both directions before trusting the classifier: (1) POSITIVE control -- feed it a handful of Hays prop_ids already known from CTX-HAYS-REBIND's own worked examples (e.g. prop_id 26199 -> QuickRefID R117015 -> PropertyNumber 11-2242-000I-02900-2) and assert the classifier resolves the SAME PropertyID; (2) NEGATIVE control -- feed it a Caldwell prop_id known to have no txgio coverage and assert it does NOT get a false different-key resolution; (3) ambiguity control -- a synthetic fixture where two export rows share a property_number, assert the classifier refuses (unknown), never guesses; (4) the completion predicate's own violation: assert that BEFORE the real-account filter is applied, disposition coverage reads (falsely) 100% complete with zero non-intersecting rows, and that this is exactly the vacuity this CP names -- the instrument's self-test must demonstrate it would have been fooled by the naive form, not merely assert its own current correctness.
